monthly_review.summary: Pace improved significantly and VO2max readings increased, but at the cost of higher average HR, declining running economy, and rising aerobic decoupling — a classic sign of accumulating fatigue masking as performance gain.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite running 12.3 km less and 2 fewer sessions than last month, average pace improved by 23 sec/km — but this came with a 6 bpm HR increase, 0.55 ml/kg/km worse running economy, and elevated aerobic TE, confirming it reflects fatigue-driven inefficiency rather than true fitness gain.

goal_tracker.message: Chasing last month’s 51.3 km is not advisable: recovery indicators are compromised, and the current trend shows diminishing returns (worsening efficiency, rising HR, lower cadence). Prioritizing recovery over volume is essential — do not add sessions or distance until readiness improves.

insights.title: Pace–HR dissociation signals autonomic strain
insights.body: Avg pace improved by 23 sec/km while avg HR rose 6 bpm — a paradox that only occurs when sympathetic drive overrides metabolic demand, commonly seen during incomplete recovery. This aligns with the jump in Z4% (27% vs 8%) and rising aerobic TE (2.9% vs 2.6%).

insights.title: Cadence collapse correlates with efficiency decline
insights.body: Cadence dropped from 149 spm (Aug) to 141 spm (Sep), while running efficiency worsened from 14.12 to 14.67 ml/kg/km — a 0.55 ml/kg/km increase (worse) — suggesting neuromuscular fatigue is impairing stride coordination and oxygen cost.

insights.title: Z4 dominance displaces foundational Z2 work
insights.body: Z4% surged to 27% this month (vs 8% in Aug and 18% in Jul), while Z1+Z2 dropped to 48% (vs 65% in Aug). This shift away from aerobic base building coincides with rising aerobic TE and falling efficiency — evidence of premature intensity without sufficient recovery or endurance foundation.

insights.title: VO2max gains appear transient and context-dependent
insights.body: VO2max readings rose from 39–40 to 42.0 in three recent runs (Sep 10, 15, 17), but occurred alongside elevated HR, lower cadence, and higher vertical oscillation (8.2–8.4 cm), suggesting measurement noise or effort-driven inflation rather than sustainable adaptation.
